<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="ניסן_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518917769_theRebbe_254" batchId="meluket-_D7_A0_D7_99_D7_A1_D7_9F_meluket__BH_POST_1766518917769_theRebbe_254__p003">
  <section v="6">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that Israel's choice of G-d over His ministers stems from the soul, which is above intellect, and that this soul-choice then influences the intellect to also choose G-d.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">6)</t>
    <t s="1">And it is necessary to understand,</t>
    <t s="2">for at first glance,</t>
    <t s="3">even according to this explanation that the choice of the clever one in the king is not because of the benefit he will have from this, but because of the king's greatness,</t>
    <t s="4">therefore he forgoes the abundance of influence that comes through them,</t>
    <t s="5">his choice in the king is from the aspect of intellect,</t>
    <t s="6">for since all of them are subject to change and the King is not subject to change, it is fitting to forgo</t>
    <t s="7">the abundance of influence that comes through the ministers and to choose the limited influence that comes from the king,</t>
    <t s="8">and from the fact that the Midrash connects this matter</t>
    <t s="9">("I will take the king")</t>
    <t s="10">with "A portion of G-d is my soul said,"</t>
    <t s="11">it implies,</t>
    <t s="12">that this that Israel chooses the Holy One, blessed be He, is from the aspect of the soul</t>
    <t s="13">(which is a portion of G-d)</t>
    <t s="14">which is above intellect.</t>
    <t s="15">And the point of the explanation in this,</t>
    <t s="16">is that the intellect of man, as it is in itself, compels him to desire only that which is good for him.</t>
    <t s="17">For this is that the nations of the world choose the ministers,</t>
    <t s="18">even though they too can understand that the king is the main thing</t>
    <t s="19">(for all of them are subject to change and the King is not subject to change),</t>
    <t s="20">because being in the aspect of yesh (somethingness),</t>
    <t s="21">they do not want to forgo the benefit they will have by receiving from the ministers.</t>
    <t s="22">And this that in Israel there is the recognition that one must forgo their benefit and their existence and choose G-dliness,</t>
    <t s="23">is from the aspect of the soul</t>
    <t s="24">(a portion of G-d)</t>
    <t s="25">whose choice in G-dliness is an intrinsic choice that is above intellect</t>
    <t s="26">(for this choice is not because of the superiority of G-dliness,</t>
    <t s="27">that the King is not subject to change,</t>
    <t s="28">but from the aspect of Atzmus (Essence)),</t>
    <t s="29">and this affects their intellect,</t>
    <t s="30">so that even the intellect recognizes that since G-dliness is the truth that lives and exists in eternal existence</t>
    <t s="31">(the King is not subject to change),</t>
    <t s="32">he must forgo his own existence and choose G-dliness.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="7">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section elaborates on four levels in serving the King—dogs, lowly servants, important servants, and ministers—corresponding to spiritual levels, and connects them to the Midrash's terms.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">7)</t>
    <t s="1">And perhaps one may add,</t>
    <t s="2">that by the choice of the soul, which is above intellect, being drawn down and affecting the intellect,</t>
    <t s="3">an even more elevated superiority is added to it beyond what it is in itself.</t>
    <t s="4">And this will be understood by prefacing what is explained in the Siddur, in the discourse "Avadim Hayinu L'Pharoh B'Mitzrayim",</t>
    <t s="5">regarding the influence that is drawn to those who transgress His will,</t>
    <t s="6">which is only in an incidental manner, like one who throws [something] behind his shoulders,</t>
    <t s="7">which is analogous to a king</t>
    <t s="8">who makes a feast and banquet for the sake of the great ministers and the important servants, and spends much money on this,</t>
    <t s="9">and from the leftovers of the feast, even those of lesser value, like servants and maidservants who are behind the millstones, also receive,</t>
    <t s="10">and even the dogs eat the bones that are thrown down.</t>
    <t s="11">Surely the king did not intend to spend for their sake,</t>
    <t s="12">and this that leftovers are bestowed upon them</t>
    <t s="13">(even the leftovers of the feast are great wealth)</t>
    <t s="14">is only incidentally.</t>
    <t s="15">And similarly in the analogy, the influence to those who transgress His will is only incidentally,</t>
    <t s="16">like one who throws [something] behind his shoulders,</t>
    <t s="17">as explained there at length.</t>
    <t s="18">And it may be said,</t>
    <t s="19">that this that he brings two examples of those whose influence is only incidentally</t>
    <t s="20">(and they do not sit at the king's table),</t>
    <t s="21">servants and maidservants and dogs,</t>
    <t s="22">and two examples of those who sit at the king's table,</t>
    <t s="23">great ministers and important servants,</t>
    <t s="24">is,</t>
    <t s="25">corresponding to four levels in the analogy.</t>
    <t s="26">That the lowest level is the dogs, who do not serve the king and whose desire is that physicality be bestowed upon them,</t>
    <t s="27">and furthermore,</t>
    <t s="28">as it is written,</t>
    <t s="29">"The dogs are of greedy soul, they know no satiety."</t>
    <t s="30">And one may connect this with the known idea</t>
    <t s="31">that "kelev" (dog) is from the term "kulo lev" (all heart).</t>
    <t s="32">For the nature of man in his birth and the nature of his formation is that the brain rules over the heart,</t>
    <t s="33">and this that he is in the aspect of a dog is at the opposite extreme.</t>
    <t s="34">For not only does the heart rule over the brain,</t>
    <t s="35">but furthermore, he is all heart.</t>
    <t s="36">And therefore all</t>
    <t s="37">his concern is to fulfill the desire of his heart.</t>
    <t s="38">And above this are the lowly servants</t>
    <t s="39">(the servants and maidservants who are behind the millstones),</t>
    <t s="40">who serve the king, but their service is only out of compulsion</t>
    <t s="41">(for fear of the striking of the rod),</t>
    <t s="42">contrary to their will and pleasure,</t>
    <t s="43">for "a servant prefers to be free."</t>
    <t s="44">And since their will and pleasure is in the desires of this world,</t>
    <t s="45">and this that they do not transgress His will, may He be blessed, is because of fear of punishment,</t>
    <t s="46">their place is outside the king's table.</t>
    <t s="47">But the important servants,</t>
    <t s="48">their service of the king is with will and desire.</t>
    <t s="49">For although the main point of their service is from the aspect of acceptance of the yoke</t>
    <t s="50">[as is known</t>
    <t s="51">the difference between a son and a servant,</t>
    <t s="52">that this that the son does his father's will is because of love, and this that the servant fulfills his master's will is in the manner of acceptance of the yoke],</t>
    <t s="53">nevertheless,</t>
    <t s="54">this very thing is with will and desire,</t>
    <t s="55">for they want to accept upon themselves the yoke of the kingdom of heaven.</t>
    <t s="56">And therefore their place is at the king's table.</t>
    <t s="57">And above them are the ministers,</t>
    <t s="58">who have knowledge of the conduct of the monarchy</t>
    <t s="59">[therefore many matters in the conduct are conducted according to them],</t>
    <t s="60">and they also have comprehension of the king's greatness, and because of this they have love for him,</t>
    <t s="61">and their service is not only from the aspect of acceptance of the yoke, but also from the aspect of love.</t>
    <t s="62">And within the ministers themselves there are many levels,</t>
    <t s="63">which are divided generally into two.</t>
    <t s="64">Ministers</t>
    <t s="65">(plain)</t>
    <t s="66">and great ministers.</t>
    <t s="67">And it may be said,</t>
    <t s="68">that these three types that are found at the king's table</t>
    <t s="69">[important servants,</t>
    <t s="70">ministers, and great ministers]</t>
    <t s="71">correspond to the three types in the Midrash,</t>
    <t s="72">Dukes, Hyparchs, and Strategoi,</t>
    <t s="73">who are found together with the king,</t>
    <t s="74">as the language of the Midrash, "and they were with him,"</t>
    <t s="75">analogous to the important servants and the ministers who are at the king's table.</t>
    <t s="76">And based on this it may be said,</t>
    <t s="77">that although the intention</t>
    <t s="78">(simply)</t>
    <t s="79">in Dukes etc. is for the ministers of Nogah</t>
    <t s="80">(as brought above from the discourses),</t>
    <t s="81">nevertheless,</t>
    <t s="82">this that he emphasizes that the Dukes "were with him" is in order to hint that he speaks here</t>
    <t s="83">[not only about the ministers of Nogah,</t>
    <t s="84">which are a yesh and a separate thing,</t>
    <t s="85">analogous to the lowly servants whose place is outside the king's table,</t>
    <t s="86">but]</t>
    <t s="87">also about the angels who are nullified to G-dliness,</t>
    <t s="88">and even higher—in the Sefiros of Atzilus, where "He and His life-force and His organs are one,"</t>
    <t s="89">which are always with the king.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="8">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section concludes that the clever one's choice of the king himself, not even the highest spiritual levels, reflects the Baal Shem Tov's teaching on prayer, requiring great cleverness.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And based on this, the greatness of the cleverness of the one who said "I will take the king" is even more understood,</t>
    <t s="1">for in addition to this that he does not want to receive influence in the manner of the dogs, and also not like the lowly servants who are outside the king's table</t>
    <t s="2">(even though the influence that is bestowed upon them is in great abundance)</t>
    <t s="3">and he wants to be at the king's table,</t>
    <t s="4">but rather he does not want even the Dukes etc.</t>
    <t s="5">(angels,</t>
    <t s="6">Sefiros of Atzilus and even higher),</t>
    <t s="7">but rather the king,</t>
    <t s="8">"I will take the king."</t>
    <t s="9">And like the well-known teaching of the Baal Shem Tov</t>
    <t s="10">on the verse,</t>
    <t s="11">"A prayer of the afflicted when he wraps himself, and before G-d he pours out his complaint,"</t>
    <t s="12">that he does not ask for anything, and his prayer is that "before G-d he pours out his complaint."</t>
    <t s="13">And for this, great cleverness is needed.</t>
    <t s="14">And analogous to a flesh-and-blood king,</t>
    <t s="15">that in order to enter the small chamber where the king is and to see the king's face,</t>
    <t s="16">one must first pass through many palaces, in each of which there is precious wealth,</t>
    <t s="17">and there are those who, when they see the precious wealth in the outer palace,</t>
    <t s="18">they delight in it with a wondrous delight and tarry there.</t>
    <t s="19">And there are those who delight in a more inner palace.</t>
    <t s="20">And specifically one who is a great wise man,</t>
    <t s="21">the importance and preciousness of the immense wealth found even in the innermost palace does not matter to him,</t>
    <t s="22">and all his will and desire is to enter the small chamber where the king is and to see the king's face.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
